title.narrative: Community Resilience through Early Action Messaging (CREAM)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Community Resilience through Early Action Messaging (CREAM) project is a targeted $100,000, 8-month intervention meticulously designed to address the intersection of climate volatility and food insecurity in the Maiduguri and Jere LGAs of Borno State. In an environment where over 5.8 million people are projected to face severe hunger (CH Phase 3+), this project functions as a critical "information-as-aid" layer that strengthens the efficacy of the broader Food Security Sector (FSS). The project moves beyond traditional weather alerts by focusing on Food Security Risk Communication—the process of translating complex climate, market, and crop data into localized, technical advisories that enable households to protect their livelihoods before disaster strikes.ltbrgtThe core strategy revolves around a robust Messaging Lifecycle. This begins with technical validation workshops where food security experts, agronomists, and climate scientists simplify complex data into "household-ready" instructions. These advisories focus on practical, protective behaviors such as early harvest techniques to avoid flood loss, humidity-controlled grain storage to prevent post-harvest spoilage, and climate-adjusted planting schedules. By operationalizing these messages through a multi-channel dissemination network—including local radio (Kanuri and Hausa), mobile SMS alerts, and public awareness campaigns—the project ensures that life-saving information reaches the "last mile."ltbrgtTo ensure deep community penetration, the project leverages the Nigerian Red Cross Society’s (NRCS) extensive volunteer base to conduct direct house-to-house (H2H) sensitization. This personal engagement is vital for addressing the needs of non-literate populations and marginalized groups, ensuring that the 250,000 target beneficiaries do not just receive a message, but fully comprehend the technical actions required to safeguard their food stocks. The establishment of Community Resilience Committees ensures that this communication flow is locally owned and sustainable.ltbrgtFurthermore, the project is built on the foundation of Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP). Through toll-free lines and community help desks, the project gathers real-time feedback to refine and adapt messaging based on community needs. This ensures that the intervention remains responsive to the evolving food security landscape. By focusing exclusively on the communication layer, CREAM provides a high-impact, low-cost force multiplier that protects the physical assets and dietary intake of vulnerable households, directly supporting the NHF’s mandate to integrate climate adaptation into the heart of food security programming. This approach transforms passive recipients of climate data into active, informed managers of their own food security and resilience.ltbrgtlt/pgt
